{{Tooltip|L|Lost}} 54–60 vs. [[2013–14 UConn Huskies men's basketball team|Connecticut]] }} {{2013–14 SEC men's basketball standings}} The '''2013–14 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Kentucky]] in the [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2013–14 college basketball season]]. The team played its home games in [[Lexington, Kentucky]] for the 39th consecutive season at [[Rupp Arena]], with a capacity of 23,500. The team was led by fifth-year head coach [[John Calipari]]. This team was nicknamed the "Tweakables" in reference to Calipari's comment prior to the [[2014 SEC men's basketball tournament|2014 SEC tournament]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nola.com/lsu/index.ssf/2014/04/kentucky_uconn_have_been_disre.html|title=Kentucky, UConn have been 'disrespected' throughout entire tournament|access-date=2015-03-16|date=2014-04-06|publisher=[[The Times Picayune]]|author=Higgins, Ron}} The team was the National Runner-up in the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], and also marked Kentucky's 16th Final Four appearance. It was Calipari's third Final Four appearance at Kentucky. Despite the [[2012–13 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|2012–13 team]] making the [[2013 NIT|NIT]], there were high expectations for this team. The team, however, would be without some of its top players from the 2012–13 team including [[Nerlens Noel]]{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041513aab.html|title=Noel to Enter NBA Draft|access-date=2015-03-16|date=2013-04-15|publisher=University of Kentucky|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402134115/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041513aab.html|archive-date=2015-04-02}} and starting shooting guard [[Archie Goodwin (basketball)|Archie Goodwin]],{{cite web|url=http://www.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/kentucky-archie-goodwin-will-enter-nba-draft-willie-cauley-stein-kyle-wiltjer-will-return-040113?gt1=39002 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20150316202558/http://www.foxsports.com/collegebasketball/story/kentucky-archie-goodwin-will-enter-nba-draft-willie-cauley-stein-kyle-wiltjer-will-return-040113?gt1=39002 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2015-03-16 |title=Kentucky's Goodwin to enter NBA draft |access-date=2015-03-16 |date=2013-06-02 |publisher=Associated Press }} who were first-round draft choices in the [[2013 NBA draft]]. Starting power forward [[Kyle Wiltjer]] transferred to [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]]{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2013/07/19/former-kentucky-player-kyle-wiltjer-transfers-to-gonzaga/2569325/|title=Former Kentucky player Kyle Wiltjer transfers to Gonzaga|access-date=2015-03-16|date=2013-07-16|website=USA Today|author=Tucker, Kyle}} and starting point guard Ryan Harrow transferred to [[Georgia State Panthers men's basketball|Georgia State]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/9117630/ryan-harrow-transferring-kentucky-wildcats-georgia-state-panthers|title=Ryan Harrow to transfer to Ga. State|access-date=2015-03-16|date=2013-05-31|publisher=ESPN}} Returning was former [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] [[Alex Poythress]] and starting center [[Willie Cauley-Stein]]. The poor success of the 2012–13 team did not stop John Calipari from again producing another number one recruiting class. The entering class included a record six McDonald's All-Americans {{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2013/03/31/kentucky-recruits-dominate-mcdonalds-all-american-game-rosters/|title=Kentucky recruits dominate McDonald's All-American game rosters|access-date=2015-03-16|date=2013-03-31|website=Chicago Tribune|author=Colleen Kane}} highlighted by [[Julius Randle]] and the Harrison Twins, [[Aaron Harrison|Aaron]] and [[Andrew Harrison (basketball)|Andrew]]. The Wildcats were led by [[2014 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2014 Consensus All-American]] and [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year]] Randle, a unanimous first-team All-SEC selection. Harrison alley oop (5).jpg | caption3 = [[Aaron Harrison]] }} {{clear}} Many recruiting analysts and experts proclaimed that the 2013 signing class for Kentucky was the greatest recruiting class since the infamous [[Fab Five (University of Michigan)|Fab Five]] in the 1990s.{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/recruiting/2013/10/29/john-calipari-kentucky-wildcats-recruiting-class-best-in-college-basketball-history/3171357/|title=Kentucky reloads: Calipari ushers in 'best ever' freshman class|access-date=2015-03-16|date=2013-10-29|website=USA Today}} Some proclaimed that it was the greatest ever assembled. It featured a record six McDonald's All-Americans and five consensus top fifteen players. Julius Randle, originally from [[Plano, Texas]], was the highest rated signee in the 2013 class. He committed to Kentucky on March 18, one day after Kentucky lost to Robert Morris in the opening round of the NIT.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/9075457/kentucky-wildcats-bounce-back-julius-randle-commitment|title=Julius Randle commits to Kentucky|access-date=2015-03-16|date=2013-03-20|publisher=ESPN}} He chose Kentucky over [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] and [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]]. He was the nation's consensus top power forward, was ranked the No. 2 overall player by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], the No. 3 overall player by [[ESPNU Recruiting Insider|ESPN]] and the No. 5 overall player by [[Scout.com|Scout]]. He helped lead [[Prestonwood Christian Academy|Prestonwood Christian]] to three state titles including one in his freshman year and back-to-back titles in junior and senior seasons. He was a McDonald's All-America and [[Jordan Brand Classic]] game selection. He was the co-MVP in the Jordan Brand Classic.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041813aad.html|title=Hawkins, Johnson and Randle join five previous additions from fall signing period|access-date=2015-03-16|date=2013-04-18|publisher=University of Kentucky|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402154457/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041813aad.html|archive-date=2015-04-02|url-status=dead}} The Harrison twins, Aaron and Andrew, became the first set of twins to ever play for Kentucky. Andrew was the consensus top point guard and Aaron was the consensus top shooting guard in the 2013 class. Out of [[Richmond, Texas]], the Twins committed to Kentucky on October 4, 2012, on a live broadcast on ESPNU.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/8462850/kentucky-wildcats-land-twin-recruits-aaron-harrison-andrew-harrison|title=Harrison twins choose Kentucky|access-date=2015-03-16|date=2012-10-05|publisher=ESPN}} The Twins chose Kentucky over their Father's alma mater, [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]]. They were a McDonald's All-America and Jordan Brand Classic game selections.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111512aab.html|title=Cats well on way to fifth straight No. 1 ranked class|access-date=2015-03-16|date=2012-11-15|publisher=University of Kentucky|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402100624/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111512aab.html|archive-date=2015-04-02|url-status=dead}} [[James Young (basketball)|James Young]] was a consensus top ten prospect within the 2013 class. Originally from [[Rochester, Michigan]], he committed to Kentucky on October 11, 2012, on ESPNU.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/8492054/james-young-no-5-prospect-2013-class-commits-kentucky-wildcats|title=James Young chooses Kentucky|access-date=2015-03-16|date=2012-10-11|publisher=ESPN}} He chose Kentucky over in-state schools [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] and [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]]. Young was ranked as the No. 6 prospect in the class by ESPN and No. 10 by both Rivals and Scout. He was a McDonald's All-America game selection. [[Dakari Johnson]] was the consensus top center in the 2013 class. He committed to Kentucky on January 5, live on ESPNU.{{cite news|url=http://blogs.courier-journal.com/recruiting/2013/01/05/5-star-c-dakari-johnson-commits-to-uk-basketball-team/|title=5-star C Dakari Johnson commits to UK basketball team|access-date=2015-03-16|date=2013-01-05|newspaper=Courier-Journal|archive-url=https://archive.today/20150318035602/http://blogs.courier-journal.com/recruiting/2013/01/05/5-star-c-dakari-johnson-commits-to-uk-basketball-team/|archive-date=2015-03-18|url-status=dead}} He chose Kentucky over [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]] and [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]]. He was rated as the No. 11 overall player by ESPN, No. 9 overall player by Rivals, and No. 18 over all player by Scout. Johnson led his high school, [[Montverde Academy|Montverde]], to a national championship at the National High School Invitational where he claimed MVP honors after logging 18 points and eight rebounds. He was a McDonald's All-America. [[Marcus Lee]] was a forward and participated several sports in high school and made all-state selections in both basketball and volleyball. He committed to Kentucky on October 17, 2012, choosing Kentucky over [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]] and [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]].{{cite news|url=http://www.contracostatimes.com/ci_21793884/basketball-star-marcus-lee-chooses-kentucky-wildcats-over|title=Basketball star Marcus Lee chooses Kentucky Wildcats over Cal|access-date=2015-03-16|date=2012-10-17|newspaper=Courier-Journal}} He was a McDonald's All-America and Jordan Brand Classic game selection. Derek Willis was the first commitment in the class of 2013. Originally committed to [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]], he opted for the Wildcats on January 20, 2012, when he was junior in high school.{{cite web|url=https://insider.espn.com/blog/ncbrecruiting/on-the-trail/post/_/id/993/junior-derek-willis-commits-to-kentucky|title=Junior Derek Willis commits to Kentucky|access-date=2015-03-16|date=2012-01-20|publisher=ESPN}} Dominique Hawkins was the least heralded of all the signees in the 2013 signing class. ''USA Today'' announced its initial coaches poll on October 18, with Kentucky ranked as No. 1 in the country.{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2013/10/17/coaches-poll-top-25-kentucky-wildcats-no-1-number-one/3001413/|title=Kentucky is No. 1 in preseason USA TODAY Sports Coaches Poll|access-date=2015-03-16|date=2013-10-18|work=USA Today}} The Associated Press announced on October 31 that Kentucky was ranked No. 1 to start the season in its initial poll of the season.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/103113aab.html|title=UK Ranked No. 1 in Associated Press Preseason Top 25|access-date=2015-03-16|date=2013-10-31|work=University of Kentucky|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402105930/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/103113aab.html|archive-date=2015-04-02}} ===Events=== On October 3 the camp out for Big Blue Madness, Kentucky's version of [[Midnight Madness (basketball)|Midnight Madness]], began. There were a record 755 tents set up around [[Memorial Coliseum (University of Kentucky)|Memorial Coliseum]] to be first in line for the tickets that went on sale for Big Blue Madness on October 5.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/100313aab.html|title=Madness Campout Sets New Mark; Control Cards Limited|access-date=2015-03-16|date=2013-10-03|work=University of Kentucky|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402162331/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/100313aab.html|archive-date=2015-04-02|url-status=dead}} Tickets for Big Blue Madness sold out on October 5 in thirty minutes.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/100513aaa.html|title=Madness Tickets SOLDOUT|access-date=2015-03-16|date=2013-10-05|work=University of Kentucky|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402090234/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/100513aaa.html|archive-date=2015-04-02|url-status=dead}} Big Blue Madness took place on October 18. The event debuted the team for the 2013–14 season. It included player introductions, a speech by Calipari, and a scrimmage.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/blog/2013/10/big-blue-madness-2013-videos.html|title=Big Blue Madness highlights|access-date=2015-03-16|date=2013-10-18|work=University of Kentucky}} The Blue-White scrimmage was the first live game for the team. It occurred at Rupp Arena on October 29. The Blue team started four freshmen, Andrew Harrison, Aaron Harrison, Young and Randle, along with Cauley-Stein. The White team opened with Jarrod Polson, Jon Hood, sophomore Poythress, Willis, and Lee. Young led all players with 21 points.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/102913aab.html|title=Blue-White Scrimmage Notes|access-date=2015-03-16|date=2013-10-29|work=University of Kentucky|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402165858/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/102913aab.html|archive-date=2015-04-02|url-status=dead}} The first exhibition game was against [[Transylvania University|Transylvania]] on November 1 at Rupp Arena.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/110113aab.html|title=Kentucky-Transylvania Postgame Notes|access-date=2015-03-16|date=2013-11-01|work=University of Kentucky|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140101081828/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/110113aab.html|archive-date=2014-01-01|url-status=dead}} Kentucky defeated Transylvania 76 to 42. Randle notched a double-double with 16 points and 12 rebounds.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2013-2014/uk1101.html|title=Kentucky-Transylvania Boxscore|access-date=2015-03-16|date=2013-11-01|work=University of Kentucky}} The second and final exhibition game was against [[Montevallo University|Montevallo]] on November 4 at Rupp Arena.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/110413aae.html|title=Kentucky-Montevallo Postgame Notes|access-date=2015-03-16|date=2013-11-04|work=University of Kentucky|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402153201/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/110413aae.html|archive-date=2015-04-02|url-status=dead}} Kentucky defeated Montevallo 95 to 72. Randle collected 21 points and 11 rebounds, giving him a double-double in both exhibition games. Young tallied 16 points and had the play of the night when he saved the ball from going out of bounds and accidentally lofted the ball into his own defensive basket, scoring two points for Montevallo.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2013-2014/uk1104.html|title=Kentucky-Montevallo Boxscore|access-date=2015-03-16|date=2013-11-04|work=University of Kentucky}} ==2014–15 signees== In November Kentucky signed another top recruiting class. John Calipari announced four players for his 2014 class during the early signing period on November 14. [[Trey Lyles]] (Indianapolis), [[Karl-Anthony Towns]] (Metuchen, N.J.), [[Devin Booker]] (Grand Rapids, Mich.) and [[Tyler Ulis]] (Chicago Heights, Ill.) all signed national letters of intent to play basketball at the University of Kentucky, starting in the 2014–15 season.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/blog/2013/11/never-count-john-calipari-out.html|title=UK, Calipari sign four for 2014|access-date=2015-03-17|date=2013-11-14|publisher=University of Kentucky|archive-date=April 2, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402132117/http://www.ukathletics.com/blog/2013/11/never-count-john-calipari-out.html|url-status=dead}} Karl-Anthony Towns was the first commitment for the class when verbally committed on December 4, 2012.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/8708701/karl-towns-jr-gives-oral-commitment-kentucky-reclassified-junior|title=Karl Towns Jr. commits to Kentucky|access-date=2015-03-17|date=2012-12-04|publisher=ESPN}} He was named [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade National Player of the Year]] in 2014.{{cite news|url=http://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2014/07/16/kentucky-basketballs-karl-anthony-towns-wins-gatorade-player-year/12727841/|title=UK's Towns named Gatorade Athlete of the Year|access-date=2015-03-17|date=2014-07-16|newspaper=Courier-Journal}} He played for the Dominican Republic National Team in 2012 and 2013 which were coached by John Calipari and Kentucky assistant, [[Orlando Antigua]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/high-school/boys-basketball/story/_/id/8001784/new-jersey-native-karl-towns-jr-16-play-dominican-republic-olympic-qualifying|title=Towns Jr. going global|access-date=2015-03-17|date=2012-06-18|publisher=ESPN}} He was ranked as No. 6 overall by ESPN and No. 11 by Rivals and Scout. Tyler Ulis was the second commitment in the class when he verbally committed on September 13, 2013.{{cite news|url=http://www.kentucky.com/2013/09/13/2820594/chicago-point-guard-ulis-commits.html|title=Chicago point guard Ulis commits to Kentucky|access-date=2015-03-17|date=2013-09-13|newspaper=Lexington Herald-Leader|author=Roberts, Ben}} He committed to Kentucky briefly after he was offered a scholarship. Kentucky had just missed on their primary target, [[Emmanuel Mudiay]], when he committed to [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|SMU]] on August 24, 2013.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/dallas/story/_/id/9597797/emmanuel-mudiay-no-2-point-guard-commits-smu-mustangs|title=Emmanuel Mudiay commits to SMU|access-date=2015-03-17|date=2013-08-24|publisher=ESPN}} Ulis, however, quickly rose the recruiting ranking finishing No. 20 overall by Scout, No. 21 overall by Rivals, and No. 25 overall by ESPN. He chose Kentucky over [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]], [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]], and [[USC Trojans men's basketball|Southern Cal]]. Devin Booker was the third commitment in the class when he verbally committed on October 31, 2013.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/9908976/devin-booker-no-18-overall-prospect-commits-kentucky-wildcats|title=Devin Booker commits to Kentucky|access-date=2015-03-17|date=2013-10-31|publisher=ESPN}} He was ranked as the No. 18 overall by ESPN and No. 29 overall by Scout and Rivals. As a junior, he was named by Gatorade as the top basketball player in Mississippi.{{cite web|url=http://www.gatorade.com/poy/assets/writable/14581/2012-13_BK_DBooker.pdf|title=Devin Booker named Player of the Year|access-date=2015-03-17|date=2013-03-08|publisher=Gatorade}} He is the son of the former [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]] and All-American great [[Melvin Booker]]. He chose Kentucky over his Dad's alma mater and Michigan. Trey Lyles was the final commitment in the class when he verbally committed on November 5, 2013.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/9930947/trey-lyles-commits-kentucky-wildcats|title=Trey Lyles commits to Kentucky|access-date=2015-03-17|date=2013-11-05|publisher=ESPN}} After his senior season, he was named [[Indiana Mr. Basketball]], where he led his high school to a state championship.{{cite news|url=http://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2014/04/08/trey-lyles-wins-indystar-mr-basketball-award/7460937/|title=Tech's Trey Lyles wins IndyStar Mr. Basketball award|access-date=2015-03-17|date=2014-04-08|newspaper=Indianapolis Star|author=Neddenriep, Kyle}} He committed to Kentucky over rivals [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] and [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]]. Randle led all scorers with 15 points and all rebounders with 15 rebounds.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/110813aaa.html|title=Kentucky Opens Season with 89-57 Win Over UNC Asheville|access-date=2013-11-08|date=2015-03-27|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131109053608/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/110813aaa.html|archive-date=2013-11-09|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400498440|title=Julius Randle, No. 1 Kentucky rout UNC-Asheville|access-date=2013-11-08|date=2015-03-27|publisher=[[ESPN]]|work=ESPN.com}} Two nights later, on November 10, the team squared off against in-state foe [[2013–14 Northern Kentucky Norse men's basketball team|Northern Kentucky]], it was the first meeting between the two schools. Kentucky prevailed 93–63 behind another strong performance from Randle.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/111013aaa.html|title=Randle Leads Kentucky Past NKU 93-63|access-date=2013-11-10|date=2015-03-27|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131111013146/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/111013aaa.html|archive-date=2013-11-11|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400499025|title=Julius Randle scores 22 to lift Kentucky in laugher |access-date=2013-11-10|date=2015-03-27|publisher=[[ESPN]]|work=ESPN.com}} Kentucky's first challenge of the season came two nights later in [[United Center|Chicago]] at the [[Champions Classic]] against No. 2 [[2013–14 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]]. November 12 was the earliest the AP No. 1 and No. 2 teams had ever met in college basketball history. Kentucky made a late rally from being down 12 at halftime but ended up losing 78–74 for their first loss of the season. Julius Randle continued to boast huge numbers by posting his third consecutive double-double, 27 points and 13 rebounds.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/111213aaa.html|title=Michigan State Edges Kentucky 78-74|access-date=2013-11-12|date=2015-03-27|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131113055300/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/111213aaa.html|archive-date=2013-11-13|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400506311|title=Michigan State tops Kentucky in battle of top-ranked teams|access-date=2013-11-12|date=2015-03-27|publisher=[[ESPN]]|work=ESPN.com}} On November 17 Kentucky avenged its 2013 NIT loss to [[2013–14 Robert Morris Colonials men's basketball team|Robert Morris]] at Rupp Arena winning 87–49 in the first game of the inaugural [[Bill Keightley]] Classic. Aaron Harrison led all scorers with 28, while Randle posted his fourth consecutive double double.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/111713aaa.html|title=Kentucky Cruises Past Robert Morris to Open Keightley Classic|access-date=2013-11-17|date=2015-03-27|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131128202230/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/111713aaa.html|archive-date=2013-11-28|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400498723|title=Top-ranked Kentucky blasts Robert Morris|access-date=2013-11-17|date=2015-03-27|publisher=[[ESPN]]|work=ESPN.com}} On November 19 the Keightley Classic continued as Kentucky defeated [[2013–14 Texas–Arlington Mavericks men's basketball team|Texas–Arlington]] 105–76. Young led all scorers with 26, Randle posted his fifth consecutive double double.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/111913aaa.html|title=Kentucky Rolls to 105-76 Win Over UT Arlington|access-date=2013-11-19|date=2015-03-27|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402123930/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/111913aaa.html|archive-date=2015-04-02|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400502345|title=James Young leads No. 4 Kentucky to rout of UT Arlington|access-date=2013-11-19|date=2015-03-27|publisher=[[ESPN]]|work=ESPN.com}} Kentucky needed a late rally to get past [[2013–14 Cleveland State Vikings men's basketball team|Cleveland State]] on November 25. Cleveland State led by 10 with 7:41 to go. Kentucky went on a 24–7 run to end the game and win 68–61.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/112513aaa.html|title=Kentucky Rallies Past Feisty Cleveland State|access-date=2013-11-25|date=2015-03-27|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131128201036/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/112513aaa.html|archive-date=2013-11-28|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400506320|title=Andrew Harrison, No. 3 Kentucky rally to escape Cleveland State|access-date=2013-11-25|date=2015-03-27|publisher=[[ESPN]]|work=ESPN.com}} Kentucky earned its 500th Rupp Arena win by beating Eastern Michigan 8163 on November 27. Kentucky's halftime lead was just 35–32, but they steadily built it to double digits with 12:52 left and led by as many as twenty-one with 2:39 remaining.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/112713aaa.html|title=Kentucky Downs Eastern Michigan, Earns 500th Rupp Arena Win|access-date=2013-11-27|date=2015-03-27|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131128201706/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/112713aaa.html|archive-date=2013-11-28|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400506322|title=No. 3 Kentucky earns 500th win at Rupp Arena over Eastern Michigan|access-date=2013-11-27|date=2015-03-27|publisher=[[ESPN]]|work=ESPN.com}} ====December==== December 1 against [[2013–14 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]] was the second consecutive season that Kentucky played at the [[Barclays Center]] in [[Brooklyn, New York|Brooklyn]]. They defeated the Friars 79 to 65 behind a near triple-double from Cauley-Stein.{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/120113aaa.html|title=Cauley-Stein's Career Night Propels Kentucky Past Providence|access-date=2013-12-01|date=2015-03-27|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=UKathletics.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131202082103/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/120113aaa.html|archive-date=2013-12-02|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400504482|title=Willie Cauley-Stein has 9 blocks in Kentucky's win over Providence|access-date=2013-12-01|date=2015-03-27|publisher=[[ESPN]]|work=ESPN.com}} Playing #20 [[2013–14 Baylor Bears basketball team|Baylor]] at [[AT&T Stadium]] on December 6 provided a chance for Kentucky to get an early glimpse into what it felt like playing at the site of 2014 Final Four. The game was a part of a double-header between the two schools. The Baylor and Kentucky women's teams played to four overtimes in which Kentucky won.
